simple.meaning: תַּמְרוּר (tamrûwr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “bitterness (plural as collective).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Jeremiah, Hosea, beginning at Jeremiah 6:26. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תַּמְרוּר (H8563) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תַּמְרוּר (tamrûwr) / H8563 is traced through Jeremiah 6:26, Jeremiah 31:15, Hosea 12:15 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Daughter of my people, clothe yourself with sackcloth, and wallow in ashes! Mourn, as for an only son, most bitter lamentation, for the destroyer will suddenly come on us.
